flags.evidence: Opened page/index.html from disk in Playwright Chromium. At 1440x900 (dpr 1) and 390x844 (dpr 1, isMobile) scrollWidth equals clientWidth (1440, 390) and no text line passes the right edge. At 390x844 with deviceScaleFactor 3 (isMobile, hasTouch) document scrollWidth is 539 vs clientWidth 390 (429 at dpr 2): fit() sets canvas.width/height to css x dpr with no CSS width, so canvas#art-cut lays out 660px wide and #art-before/#art-after 462px, widening the .steps grid column to 384px (step boxes run x=16 to 400). In #how, text lines run past the 390px viewport: step 2 h3 'Each square is matched to a thread you can buy' first line ends at x=398, step 1 p.small 'You pick the stitch count... so fine lines get blurred' ends at x=397, step 3 p.small 'A stem, an eye, a whisker...' ends at x=395. Screenshot at visual-viewport pageLeft 0 shows the heading cut as 'Each square is matched to a threa' and the paragraph as '...so fine lines ge'; the text is only fully visible after panning sideways (scrollIntoView panned the visual viewport to pageLeft 10, removing the left gutter). The 660px canvas grid itself is also cut off at the right. These are a heading and running body text, not a decorative element or footer/legal small print, so it meets HF3 (text cut off / reachable only by scrolling sideways at 390x844).
